Government Defends IDBI Bank Stake Sale Valuation Process

The Ministry of Finance has publicly defended the valuation and bidding mechanics surrounding the strategic disinvestment of IDBI Bank. According to official statements, the specific procedures utilized by authorities successfully increased the overall transaction value by ₹3,917 crore.

The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) previously approved the strategic sale of a combined 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Canadian investment firm Fairfax Financial Holdings. The transaction carries an estimated valuation of approximately ₹53,000 crore, with the approved bid price established at ₹81 per share.

Structure of the Bidding and Valuation Methodology

Addressing questions regarding procedural execution, the ministry noted that the Core Group of Secretaries on Disinvestment (CGD) was granted special powers by the CCEA to oversee the final round of bidding and resolve procedural matters. The ministry clarified that the baseline reserve price remained unchanged throughout the process, noting that initial bids were not approved and that the first round became functus officio.

The initial bidding phase took place in the 2025-26 financial year under the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) guidelines. Because DIPAM relies on indicative guidelines rather than fixed statutory rules for such situations, special authorities were delegated to the CGD.

The valuation framework utilized independent agencies operating contemporaneously to assess enterprise value. The ministry emphasized the confidentiality of the framework, describing it as "double blind" because bidders were kept unaware of the official valuation, while independent valuators did not see the submitted bids. Only the CGD reviewed the complete picture to evaluate bid reasonableness against fair valuation benchmarks.

Accounting for Liabilities and Transaction Value

To encourage higher offers, officials incorporated provisions for disputed tax demands as indemnities—a common request from qualified bidders. The ministry stated that this potential liability amounted to ₹,627 crore, while the bid-discovered price improved by ₹3,917 crore, effectively enhancing the total value for the government and the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC).

Furthermore, the ministry noted the evolving regulatory classification of the institution. IDBI Bank transitioned to a government-controlled bank in 2019 following an acquisition by LIC. While the Reserve Bank of India treated it as a private entity for regulatory purposes, ownership remained predominantly with the government and LIC.

Practical Implications and Verification

Readers and stakeholders analyzing the transaction can review several confirmed elements against ongoing uncertainties:

  • Confirmed Facts: The CCEA approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake to Fairfax Financial Holdings at ₹81 per share, totaling approximately ₹53,000 crore. The Ministry of Finance confirmed that the valuation adjustments and indemnity structures yielded a net increase in transaction value.
  • What Remains Unknown: Final closing timelines and specific post-transaction operational milestones for the private acquisition have not been fully detailed in the immediate release.
  • How to Verify: Readers can review the official context, disclosures, and related updates directly through the [Business Standard Report](https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/idbi-bank-stake-sale-government-valuation-defends-bidding-process-deal-value-126103000338_1.html) and official Ministry of Finance releases.
